item.title: Steelers release Aaron Rodgers after criticism of Mike McCarthy
item.description: The Steelers released Aaron Rodgers one day after benching him, a significant escalation after the quarterback said coach Mike McCarthy fell asleep during team meetings. Rodgers, 42, had led Pittsburgh to a 5-6 record in his second season with the club. Reuters reported the dispute and the team’s decision.

item.title: MLB sues players union as December 1 lockout approaches
item.description: Major League Baseball asked a federal court to declare its planned December 1 lockout lawful under antitrust law, seeking to head off a possible union challenge. The unusual preemptive suit underscores how far owners and players remain apart as the collective bargaining agreement nears expiration.

item.title: NBA unveils €10 billion arena plan for European league
item.description: The NBA announced a plan backed by global investors to commit at least €10 billion to new and renovated arenas and entertainment districts across Europe. The initiative would support the NBA-FIBA professional league ecosystem targeted for 2027, a major step toward the league’s long-discussed European expansion.

item.title: Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers and turn to Mason Rudolph
item.description: Pittsburgh will make Aaron Rodgers inactive and start Mason Rudolph against Denver on Friday, Reuters reported. The 6-4 Steelers remain in playoff contention, but Rodgers has completed 60.9% of his passes with an 86.6 rating. The move puts a decorated veteran on the sideline at a pivotal point in the season.

item.title: Jannik Sinner faces extended layoff after knee surgery
item.description: Jannik Sinner underwent surgery in Finland on the iliotibial band in his right knee and could miss up to four months, putting his Australian Open participation in doubt. The procedure followed a persistent problem that had limited the former world No. 1 and reshapes the opening stretch of the 2027 tennis season.

item.title: United States will host the 2028 Copa América
item.description: CONMEBOL and Concacaf confirmed that the United States will stage the 2028 Copa América from June 9 through July 9. The 16-team field will include all 10 South American associations and six Concacaf qualifiers. Host cities and stadiums will be announced later.

item.title: FIFA confirms hosts for the 2031 and 2035 Women’s World Cups
item.description: FIFA appointed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the expanded 48-team Women’s World Cup in 2031. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the 2035 tournament. Both unopposed bids were approved by acclamation at an extraordinary congress.

item.title: Players answer MLB’s salary-cap demand with full media-revenue sharing
item.description: One week before an expected lockout, the players’ union proposed equal sharing of all media revenue among MLB’s 30 clubs without a salary cap. AP’s Ronald Blum reports owners countered with a $1 million minimum salary for 2027 and bonuses, but the central dispute remains unresolved.

item.title: Commanders stun Bengals with last-second field goal
item.description: Jayden Daniels hit rookie Antonio Williams for gains of 22 and 42 yards in the final minute, setting up Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal as time expired in Washington’s 22-20 upset of Cincinnati. Stevens made five field goals, and the 4-5-1 Commanders kept their season alive.

item.title: Mets agree to record $450 million deal with Tarik Skubal
item.description: Two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets, an AP source said. The deal, pending a physical, would set pitcher records for total value and $50 million average salary. AP reported a full no-trade clause and a $45 million signing bonus.

item.title: Tom Jackson, Broncos great and ESPN mainstay, dies at 75
item.description: Tom Jackson, a leader of Denver’s Orange Crush defense and Chris Berman’s longtime partner on ESPN’s NFL Primetime, died Friday at 75. The three-time Pro Bowler played 14 seasons for the Broncos, then spent 32 years at ESPN helping define how a generation watched Sunday highlights.

item.title: Russia’s return to international sports meets European resistance
item.description: Russia’s push to re-enter international competition is colliding with visa denials, boycotts and legal challenges across Europe. Reuters reports a December 15 CAS ruling could shape participation ahead of the 2027 European Games, a key qualifying route for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

item.title: Kansas City Current capture first NWSL championship
item.description: Kansas City defeated the Washington Spirit 2-1 to win the club’s first NWSL championship. Vanessa DiBernardo scored in the first half and Debinha converted a second-half penalty before Croix Bethune’s late goal made the finish tense. The title caps a landmark season for the Current.

item.title: Nebraska stuns No. 16 Ohio State and ends 31-game ranked skid
item.description: Nebraska beat No. 16 Ohio State 31-28, ending a 31-game losing streak against AP Top 25 opponents that dated to 2016. Anthony Colandrea threw three touchdown passes as the Cornhuskers dealt a severe blow to the Buckeyes’ College Football Playoff hopes.

item.title: Wembanyama makes NBA history in 50-point Spurs rout
item.description: Victor Wembanyama had 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals as San Antonio beat New Orleans 114-91. He became the first player since the three-point line began to combine 50 points, five blocks and five made threes, adding another unprecedented line to his young career.
